headline: Human rights champion Navi Pillay wins Nobel Peace Prize
summary: The South African lawyer and former UN High Commissioner for Human Rights was honored for her work in prosecuting war crimes and genocide.
details: South Africa's Navi Pillay has been awarded the Nobel Peace Prize. The prize committee in Oslo announced the decision on Friday.
The Norwegian Nobel Committee chair, Jorgen Watne Frydnes, stated that Pillay has been instrumental in ensuring that war crimes, crimes against humanity, and genocide are prosecuted.
Pillay's distinguished career includes heading the Rwanda genocide tribunal, where she played a critical role in seeking justice for victims.
Last year, she accused Israel of genocide in Gaza, continuing her lifelong commitment to holding powerful actors accountable for human rights violations.
The United Nations described the award as a testimony to the value of human rights in the world today.
Shabia Mantoo, a spokesperson for the UN human rights agency, called the award 'wonderful' and emphasized the urgent need for human rights protections globally.
caption:
From the Rwanda genocide tribunal to Gaza, Navi Pillay has spent her life fighting for justice.

South Africa's Navi Pillay has been awarded the Nobel Peace Prize. The prize committee in Oslo announced the decision on Friday.

The Norwegian Nobel Committee chair, Jorgen Watne Frydnes, stated that Pillay has been instrumental in ensuring that war crimes, crimes against humanity, and genocide are prosecuted.

Pillay's distinguished career includes heading the Rwanda genocide tribunal, where she played a critical role in seeking justice for victims.

Last year, she accused Israel of genocide in Gaza, continuing her lifelong commitment to holding powerful actors accountable for human rights violations.

The United Nations described the award as a testimony to the value of human rights in the world today.

Shabia Mantoo, a spokesperson for the UN human rights agency, called the award 'wonderful' and emphasized the urgent need for human rights protections globally.

headline: RU probe body recommends suspension of 4 students over journalist attack
summary: The students, including Chhatra Dal leaders, were implicated in an attack on journalists at Shaheed Ziaur Rahman Hall.
details: A probe committee at Rajshahi University (RU) has recommended the temporary suspension of four students following an attack on journalists at Shaheed Ziaur Rahman Hall.
The recommended students include Ahsan Habib, Hasibul Islam Hasib, and Bishal Chakraborty—all Chhatra Dal leaders—and Ariful Islam, the general secretary of the hall parliament.
RU Vice-Chancellor Prof Faridul Islam announced the recommendations during a press briefing, noting that the probe committee submitted its report within 72 hours.

Additionally, the committee has recommended further investigation into four other students, including Chhatra Dal vice-president Takbir Ahmed Emon and RUCSU assistant cultural affairs secretary Rakibul Islam.
Three other Chhatra Dal members, Bulbul Rahman, Shariful Islam, and Shahriar Alam, have been recommended for warnings.
The probe convener, Prof Rezaul Karim, stated that Ariful Islam and Rakibul played roles in instigating the incident.
caption:
4 students face suspension at Rajshahi University after a probe committee finds them responsible for attacking journalists.

A probe committee at Rajshahi University (RU) has recommended the temporary suspension of four students following an attack on journalists at Shaheed Ziaur Rahman Hall.

The recommended students include Ahsan Habib, Hasibul Islam Hasib, and Bishal Chakraborty—all Chhatra Dal leaders—and Ariful Islam, the general secretary of the hall parliament.

RU Vice-Chancellor Prof Faridul Islam announced the recommendations during a press briefing, noting that the probe committee submitted its report within 72 hours.

Additionally, the committee has recommended further investigation into four other students, including Chhatra Dal vice-president Takbir Ahmed Emon and RUCSU assistant cultural affairs secretary Rakibul Islam.

Three other Chhatra Dal members, Bulbul Rahman, Shariful Islam, and Shahriar Alam, have been recommended for warnings.

The probe convener, Prof Rezaul Karim, stated that Ariful Islam and Rakibul played roles in instigating the incident.
